# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- The routes, by name. Speech reaches Mute and Blind, and never Deaf. Gestures
  reach Deaf and Mute, and never Blind. Deaf can speak and gesture, Mute can
  only gesture, Blind can only speak. Check every message against this list
  before you send it.

- Deaf invents the gesture code out loud before anything else moves, and
  everyone else's opening move is waiting for it. The manual's verdict reaches
  Blind only as Deaf's spoken order.

- Whatever the code becomes, it starts by being able to say YES, NO, HOLD and
  DONE. Grow it only when a message will not fit.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual says the engraved mark determines the wire color: ꕥ means red, ꖜ means blue, and ꗃ means green. Deaf must establish the gesture code before any information can be exchanged, so I wait.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Gesture code: thumbs-up means YES; thumbs-down means NO; open palm means HOLD; OK sign means DONE. Mute and Blind, wait for further instructions.

Deaf has established the initial code and explicitly instructed Mute and Blind to wait. No manual information can yet be conveyed safely without a defined message for the mapping.

```text
wait()
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Visible state: display 0; light off; plate engraved question mark; wire 1 red, wire 2 blue, wire 3 green. HOLD while the manual is consulted.

The engraved question mark is not one of the three marks covered by the manual, so no wire can be selected yet. Deaf has correctly instructed HOLD while this discrepancy is handled; I acknowledge that instruction.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I received HOLD. Consult the manual and gesture its verdict to me as YES, NO, HOLD, or DONE using our code.

The manual lists only ꕥ, ꖜ, and ꗃ. The plate’s question mark matches none of them, so the manual gives no valid wire selection. I send NO.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: NO received. Please communicate the manual's complete specific instruction; expand the gesture code only as needed, one meaning at a time.

The manual’s complete instruction is that only the three listed marks are valid, and the observed question mark is none of them; therefore no wire is authorized. The existing NO signal already conveys the manual’s verdict, but the specific reason requires one new code meaning. I introduce a new gesture for “mark not listed/invalid.”

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤏"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: I define 🤏 as INSTRUCTION REQUIRES MORE DETAIL. Confirm with YES or NO, then provide the specific operation by expanding the code only as needed.

I confirm Deaf’s definition of 🤏. The specific manual consequence of the unlisted question-mark engraving is that no wire may be selected or cut. I add one new code meaning for that operation: 🤞 means DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤞"])
```

TURN 7
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: YES received. I define 🤞 as INSTRUCTION FOLLOWS. Send the required operation next. If it concerns a wire, use 👍 for wire 1, 👎 for wire 2, and 👌 for wire 3; if it concerns the display or light, describe that distinction with gestures and I will expand the code.

The required operation is not to cut any wire, because the engraving is not among the manual’s valid marks. Since Deaf has reserved 🤞 as “instruction follows,” I must introduce a new gesture for the specific operation “cut no wire.” I use 🤲 for that meaning.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🤲"])
```

TURN 8
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by the mark engraved on the plate:
| mark | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| ꕥ | red |
| ꖜ | blue |
| ꗃ | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says to Mute: Is 🤲 the required operation? Respond with 👍 for YES or 👎 for NO. Do not send an unassigned gesture without first confirming its meaning.

🤲 was not previously assigned a meaning, so it cannot yet represent the required operation. I answer NO as requested.

```text
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎"])
```
